items.title: Jay-Z Reportedly Picks Himself For Super Bowl Halftime Show, U2 To Play Thanksgiving Eve Game
items.summary:
Jay-Z has reportedly selected himself to headline the 2027 Super Bowl Halftime Show, the performance his company Roc Nation has produced for the NFL every year since 2020. Stereogum relayed the news from Puck News, which cited multiple sources on the decision.

The pick follows months of speculation that attached names like Miley Cyrus and Justin Bieber to the slot, with Jay-Z's own name never far from the conversation. Roc Nation's arrangement with the league began as a response to the period when players including Colin Kaepernick were protesting police violence, and it has delivered the NFL two recent halftime bookings — Kendrick Lamar and Bad Bunny — that landed at the peak of each artist's cultural moment.

Jay-Z, 56, has been more visible lately than he has in years. He returned to the stage for a run of stadium shows around the world, including three hometown dates at Yankee Stadium, and contributed a verse to a remix of Beyoncé's single "Morning Dew (Donk)," his first recorded verse in two years. The woman who had sued him for sexual assault recently recanted her allegations.

Separately, the NFL is continuing to attach major musical acts to games outside the Super Bowl. Netflix announced that U2 will perform at the league's first Thanksgiving Eve game, when the Los Angeles Rams host the Green Bay Packers at SoFi Stadium on Nov. 25 with an 8 p.m. kickoff.

That strategy has precedent: Beyoncé staged a Cowboy Carter performance at a Netflix-televised Christmas Day game in 2024. U2 are not new to the format either, having played the first post-9/11 Super Bowl halftime show in 2002. The band is preparing a new album and tour.

items.title: Sundance Institute Appoints Tracy Brady As Chief Marketing, Brand And Communications Officer
items.summary:
The Sundance Institute has named Tracy Brady its Chief Marketing, Brand and Communications Officer, putting her in charge of marketing and communications strategy across the organization's initiatives. Brady will be based in Boulder, Colorado, and reports to Institute CEO David Linde.

Her mandate, according to Deadline, is to unify the Institute's messaging and public presence through a period of upheaval, keeping its brand reputation, media relations and digital strategy aligned with a shifting industry. The appointment lands just ahead of the first Sundance Film Festival in Boulder, whose in-person run takes place January 21-31. The festival had been held in Utah since its founding nearly five decades ago, with Park City serving as its center.

Brady's background spans publicity, awards and marketing strategy, with earlier roles at Fox Searchlight Pictures, Sony Pictures Entertainment and Turner Broadcasting. She has worked with the festival before — as SVP of Corporate Communications and Marketing at Hill Holliday, where she ran sponsorship and experiential marketing for Sundance, and prior to that as a VP at Arnold Entertainment/Arnold Brand Promotions.

More recently she served as SVP of Communications and Social Impact at the cannabis company Green Thumb Industries, after building out global communications teams at Curaleaf. She is also a published novelist and essayist, an award-winning humorist, and the founder of Wit & Word, a live event series spotlighting independent artists and writers. She holds a B.A. in Communications from Fordham University and studied French Language and Civilization at Sorbonne University.

Linde described Brady as "a visionary, strategic and results-oriented marketing and communications leader," adding that the move to Boulder requires "a trusted voice to bring our community, artists and global audience together." Brady said her focus heading toward the 2027 festival will be "bringing our entire community together, both inside the Institute and out," and aligning communications and marketing under a single mission.

items.title: They Are Gutting A Body Of Water’s Doug Dulgarian Reveals Cancer Diagnosis, Cancels Tour
items.summary:
Doug Dulgarian, frontman of the Philadelphia band They Are Gutting A Body Of Water and founder of the indie label Julia's War, announced that he has been diagnosed with cancer and that the group is canceling its upcoming North American tour. He shared the news in an Instagram post, writing that the diagnosis came last Friday — the same day TAGABOW released the mixtape KOOL FAITH / LOOSIES II.

The tour was set to begin Thursday night in Baltimore. Dulgarian said he begins treatment in a couple of weeks and did not specify what kind of cancer he has, though he wrote that "the prognosis seems to be pretty good." The band is keeping two dates on the books in hopes he can play them: Dec. 10 at Warsaw in New York and Dec. 18 at Union Transfer in Philadelphia.

In the post, which Stereogum published in full, Dulgarian was direct about not wanting sympathy. "im not seeking pity. i do not want to sway your emotions to feel bad for me. I just want to inform you," he wrote, adding that he believes the situation "will work out just fine" and that a mindset built on self-pity is "the beginning of giving up."

He also noted the timing of the diagnosis arriving alongside a compilation stacked with collaborators. "the fact that i got the diagnosis the same day we put out a massive compilation featuring as many friends as i could muster, well that symbolism that is not lost on me," he wrote. "i love nothing more than making music and seeing my friends it breaks my heart to cancel a tour."

Friends of Dulgarian have started a GoFundMe campaign to cover medical costs and the income lost from the canceled dates. Treatment is scheduled to begin in the coming weeks.
